name: User
rationale: The schema needs a common principal type for authenticated iTrust users.
plain_english_summary: A person who can log in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated user

name: HCP
rationale: HCP is a role-specific principal in the requirements.
plain_english_summary: A health care provider user of iTrust.
source_excerpt: HCP

name: LHCP
rationale: LHCP is a specialized provider principal referenced by creation, hospital assignment, provider-list, and designation requirements.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health care provider in iTrust.
source_excerpt: LHCP

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrator is a principal role with personnel creation and session-configuration authority.
plain_english_summary: An iTrust admin user.
source_excerpt: administrator

name: Patient
rationale: Patient is both a principal role and an important resource whose records and provider relationships are protected.
plain_english_summary: A patient represented in iTrust.
source_excerpt: patient

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representative is a principal role that can view records for represented patients.
plain_english_summary: A user authorized to act for a patient.
source_excerpt: personal representative

name: UAP
rationale: UAP users are created by LHCPs and are an explicit actor type.
plain_english_summary: A user with the UAP role in iTrust.
source_excerpt: UAP

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are personnel that administrators can create and enter as users.
plain_english_summary: An emergency responder user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: emergency responders

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are personnel that administrators can create and enter as users.
plain_english_summary: A public health agent user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: public health agents

name: Hospital
rationale: Hospitals are resources to which LHCPs can be assigned.
plain_english_summary: A hospital associated with providers in iTrust.
source_excerpt: hospitals

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records are protected resources viewed by patients and personal representatives.
plain_english_summary: A patient's health record in iTrust.
source_excerpt: medical records

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: The owner patient must be explicit so policies can enforce own-record and represented-patient access.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose medical record this is.
source_excerpt: their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Use action context patient; rejected because medical records are persistently patient-owned resources.

name: MedicalRecord__includesFamilyHistory
rationale: Family history is specifically included in medical-record viewing requirements.
plain_english_summary: Whether this record includes family history information.
source_excerpt: medical records including family history
alternatives_considered: Model FamilyHistory as a separate resource; rejected because the prose treats it as included in medical records.

name: MedicalRecord__hasPersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is a named portion of records that users may see.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains personal health information.
source_excerpt: patient personal health information
alternatives_considered: Model PersonalHealthInformation as a separate resource; rejected for this slice because it is described as content within records.

name: MedicalRecord__hasImmunizations
rationale: Immunizations are a named portion of records that users may see.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains immunization information.
source_excerpt: immunizations
alternatives_considered: Model Immunization as a separate resource; rejected for this slice because the requirement is about seeing record contents.

name: MedicalRecord__hasOfficeVisitInformation
rationale: Office-visit information is a named portion of records that users may see.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains office-visit information.
source_excerpt: office-visit information
alternatives_considered: Model OfficeVisit as a separate resource; rejected because this requirement names office-visit information inside records.

name: DemographicInformation
rationale: Demographic information is listed as an important protected resource.
plain_english_summary: A patient's demographic profile information.
source_excerpt: demographic information

name: DemographicInformation__patient
rationale: Demographic data is patient-specific and needs an owner link.
plain_english_summary: The patient this demographic information describes.
source_excerpt: patient data
alternatives_considered: Put demographic fields directly on Patient; rejected because demographic information is named as an important resource.

name: DemographicInformation__name
rationale: The HCP initially provides the patient's name.
plain_english_summary: The patient's name.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.
alternatives_considered: Put name directly on Patient; rejected to keep demographic information as the protected resource named by the spec.

name: DemographicInformation__email
rationale: The HCP initially provides the patient's email.
plain_english_summary: The patient's email address.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.
alternatives_considered: Put email directly on Patient; rejected to keep demographic information as the protected resource named by the spec.

name: Patient__mid
rationale: MID is the patient identifier and is explicitly non-editable in patient data.
plain_english_summary: The patient's medical identifier.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.
alternatives_considered: Store MID only in Credentials; rejected because the prose also refers to the patient's MID as part of patient data.

name: Credentials
rationale: Credentials capture MID/password and secret authentication fields subject to login, password-change, and secrecy requirements.
plain_english_summary: A user's login and secret credential information.
source_excerpt: credentials

name: Credentials__user
rationale: Credentials are tied to the user who authenticates with them.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns these credentials.
source_excerpt: A user enters their MID and their password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.
alternatives_considered: Put password fields directly on User; rejected because credentials are named as an important resource.

name: Credentials__mid
rationale: MID is entered during role-based login.
plain_english_summary: The login MID for the credential set.
source_excerpt: A user enters their MID and their password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

name: Credentials__hasPassword
rationale: Password existence must be representable without exposing the password value.
plain_english_summary: Whether the credential set has a password.
source_excerpt: password
alternatives_considered: Store password as String; rejected because the requirements emphasize password secrecy.

name: Credentials__hasSecurityQuestion
rationale: The security question is a credential secret that HCPs must not enter, edit, or view.
plain_english_summary: Whether the credential set has a security question.
source_excerpt: security question
alternatives_considered: Store securityQuestion as String; rejected because the requirements emphasize that HCPs must not view it.

name: Session
rationale: A session entity is needed to model authentication lifecycle and inactivity disabling for protected actions.
plain_english_summary: An authenticated iTrust session.
source_excerpt: sessions

name: Session__user
rationale: A session belongs to the authenticated user whose actions it authorizes.
plain_english_summary: The user logged into this session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__isActive
rationale: Authorization must be disabled after logout, close, or inactivity expiry.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is currently active.
source_excerpt: after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled
alternatives_considered: Use only lastActivityAt; rejected because policies need a direct active/expired boundary.

name: Session__lastActivityAt
rationale: Inactivity termination depends on session activity timing.
plain_english_summary: The last time the session was active.
source_excerpt: Electronic sessions must terminate after the configured inactivity period

name: Session__inactivityPeriodSeconds
rationale: The configured inactivity period must be available for session-expiry authorization checks.
plain_english_summary: How long a session may be inactive before it expires.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.
alternatives_considered: Create a global InactivityConfiguration entity; rejected for this slice because the session boundary can carry the configured value.

name: ProviderList
rationale: Provider lists are resources patients can view and update by adding providers.
plain_english_summary: A patient's list of providers.
source_excerpt: provider lists

name: ProviderList__patient
rationale: Provider-list operations are patient-specific and require an owner link.
plain_english_summary: The patient who owns this provider list.
source_excerpt: their provider list

name: ProviderList__providers
rationale: A provider list contains LHCP/HCP providers added by the patient.
plain_english_summary: The providers on the patient's list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list
alternatives_considered: Use Set<LHCP>; rejected because the prose says LHCP/HCP.

name: ProviderDesignation
rationale: DLHCP is patient-specific, so the designation relationship must be modeled explicitly rather than as only a global role.
plain_english_summary: A patient's designation of a provider as a designated LHCP.
source_excerpt: provider designations

name: ProviderDesignation__patient
rationale: The designation applies for a particular patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient for whom the provider is designated.
source_excerpt: for that patient

name: ProviderDesignation__provider
rationale: The designation identifies the LHCP designated as DLHCP.
plain_english_summary: The LHCP designated for the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient
alternatives_considered: Model DLHCP as a separate principal type; rejected because the spec says designation is for that patient.

name: ProviderDesignation__isDesignated
rationale: Designation and undesignation require a lifecycle state for the relationship.
plain_english_summary: Whether this provider is currently designated for the patient.
source_excerpt: can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient
alternatives_considered: Delete the ProviderDesignation on undesignation; rejected because an explicit state supports authorization checks and auditability.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Access logs are resources patients can view for their own access history.
plain_english_summary: A log of accesses to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: access logs

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Access logs are patient-owned resources.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this is.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log.

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: The access-log result includes the accessor name.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the patient's information.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Reference accessor as User; rejected because the stated result field is accessor name.

name: AccessLog__accessorRoleRelativeToPatient
rationale: The access-log result includes the accessor role relative to the patient.
plain_english_summary: The accessor's relationship or role for this patient.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Use an enum role type; rejected because the spec does not enumerate all relative roles.

name: AccessLog__accessTimestamp
rationale: The access-log result includes the access timestamp.
plain_english_summary: When the access happened.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: The access-log result includes transaction type.
plain_english_summary: What kind of access or transaction occurred.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Use an enum transaction type; rejected because the spec does not list the allowed values.

name: LHCP__specialty
rationale: Administrators must specify specialty for new LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: The medical specialty of an LHCP.
source_excerpt: The administrator must specify the specialty for a new LHCP.

name: LHCP__hospitals
rationale: Administrators can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals associated with this LHCP.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.
alternatives_considered: Model each assignment as a separate entity; rejected because this slice only requires membership in multiple hospitals.

name: PersonalRepresentative__representedPatients
rationale: Representative access depends on which patients the user represents.
plain_english_summary: The patients this personal representative may act for.
source_excerpt: patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Use only action context; rejected because the representative relationship is reusable across multiple record-view actions.
